title: Initiative Triage, Escalation, and Elastic Capacity Playbook for Company OKRs
creator: Marcus Liu
description: A single-playbook process to triage company-level initiative proposals against OKRs, provide escalation paths for contested priorities, and create an elastic capacity pool to enable opportunistic delivery without blocking existing commitments.
background: As usage of Redwood's Dedicated and Private products accelerates, multiple teams submit company-level initiatives that compete for finite engineering and platform resources. Current intake relies on ad hoc prioritization in leadership syncs; this causes friction, delayed rollouts, and frequent scope churn. We need a repeatable, auditable protocol that ties initiatives to OKRs, provides clear escalation paths, and allows short-term elastic capacity allocation for high-value bets.
objectives: Define a weighted triage rubric that maps initiative attributes (customer impact, revenue enablement, risk reduction, strategic fit, runway) to an OKR contribution score
Establish a three-tier escalation matrix with decision owners, timelines, and automatic tagging when conflicts appear
Design an 'Elastic Capacity Pool' policy that frees up 5-10% engineering capacity per quarter for validated high-leverage initiatives
Ship an intake form + lightweight automation that surfaces conflicts and simulates capacity impact in the roadmap planner
Create dashboard views in the Console for transparency: initiative scorecards, escalation status, and capacity utilization
scope: Company-level initiatives that directly map to OKRs and require cross-team coordination (product, infra, research, GTM). Includes intake form, scoring rubric, escalation runbook, elastic capacity policy, and dashboard prototypes.
out_of_scope: Single-team sprint requests, tactical bugfixes, and customer-specific support tickets. Deep financial modeling of headcount changes (we assume capacity is allocated from existing squads).
proposal_summary: 1) Intake form with mandatory fields (OKR linkage, expected MRR impact, SLO/SLA changes, risk profile). 2) Automated scoring engine that computes OKR contribution and flags conflicts. 3) Escalation matrix (Tier 1: Product Council, Tier 2: Exec Review, Tier 3: CEO arbitration) with SLAs for decisions. 4) Elastic Capacity Pool: defined budget of 5% engineering FTE credits per quarter, awarded via a weekly 'capacity auction' reviewed by Product Council. 5) Roadmap planner integration to simulate capacity and propose rollouts/canaries.
milestones: Milestone 1 - Intake & Rubric v0 (2026-03-20): finalize fields and scoring weights
Milestone 2 - Escalation Runbook v0 (2026-04-05): decision owners and SLAs documented
Milestone 3 - Elastic Capacity Policy Draft (2026-04-20): legal and finance sign-off path identified
Milestone 4 - Prototype Automation + Roadmap Integration (2026-05-10): feature-flagged UI and simulation
Milestone 5 - Console Dashboard Beta (2026-05-30): public for internal teams; telemetry enabled
Milestone 6 - Pilot Quarter & Retrospective (2026-06-30): run one quarter and collect feedback
acceptance_criteria: Intake form available and used by >90% of new company-level initiative submissions
Automated scoring produces OKR contribution score for every intake and surfaces top-3 conflicts
Escalation runbook demonstrates decision timelines (<=7 business days for Tier 1)
Elastic Capacity Pool policy is signed off by Finance + Eng leadership and applied to 1 pilot initiative
Console dashboard shows real-time capacity utilization, initiative scorecards, and escalation state
risks: Perception of unfairness if elastic capacity is repeatedly won by same teams — mitigated by max consecutive wins rule
Overcommitment of engineering squads if capacity pool allocation is not strictly enforced — mitigated by budgeted FTE credit system
Escalation fatigue for leaders during high-conflict periods — mitigated by clear triage thresholds and delegation
Complexity of integrating scoring into roadmap planner may delay automation — mitigation: ship manual CSV import first
decisions: Adopt 5% engineering capacity target for Elastic Capacity Pool for Q2 pilot
Use a 5-factor weighted rubric (customer impact 30%, revenue 25%, risk reduction 20%, strategic fit 15%, estimated effort 10%)
Escalation tiers and SLAs agreed: Tier1=Product Council (7bd), Tier2=Exec (10bd), Tier3=CEO (3bd emergency)
open_questions: Should elastic capacity be taken from every squad proportionally or from a central platform team?
How to account for cross-quarter initiatives that consume more than one quarter of elastic capacity?
What telemetry is sufficient to detect repeated unfair allocation patterns?

implementation_notes: Start with CSV-based import to validate scoring before investing in roadmap API integration
Elastic capacity accounting implemented as FTE credits per squad; engineering to build enforcement hooks in sprint planners
Telemetry: track wins by team, average time-to-decision, and variance in score vs. outcome for bias detection
test_plan: Run 10 historical initiatives through rubric offline and compare rubric ranking to leadership decisions
Simulate capacity allocation with 3 triage rounds to ensure enforcement prevents >100% allocation
UX test intake form with 6 PMs and 4 engineering leads; iterate before automation
retro_signals: Usage (>80% of new initiatives use intake) and satisfaction (survey >70% approval) measured after pilot
Reduction in unplanned scope churn measured by number of roadmap rollbacks
communication_plan: Announcement to company and execs at next All Hands with link to playbook
Weekly digest to Product Council during pilot with capacity auction results
Template email for teams when their initiative is accepted, deferred, or escalated
